description: Variable SHADOWING across nested blocks, reduced to its simplest form: a same-named DECLARE inside a nested block holds only INSIDE that block, and the statement after it sees the outer value again. Pinned at one level (5 / 20 / 5) and at two (5 / 20 / 100 / 20 / 5), which is what shows the restore happening at EACH level rather than only at the outermost. Converted 1:1 from scripting/SimpleShadowingTest (now retired); the Java's first test read the rows ORDERED BY VALUE, which sorted 5/20/5 into 5/5/20 and hid the sequence - the converted tests add a sequence column and pin the INSERT ORDER, which is the claim.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE results (seq INTEGER, value INTEGER)
DECLARE x INTEGER := 5; BEGIN INSERT INTO results VALUES (1, :x); DECLARE x INTEGER := 20; BEGIN INSERT INTO results VALUES (2, :x); END; INSERT INTO results VALUES (3, :x); END;
SELECT value FROM results ORDER BY seq
CREATE TABLE results (seq INTEGER, value INTEGER)

DECLARE x INTEGER := 5; BEGIN INSERT INTO results VALUES (1, :x); DECLARE x INTEGER := 20; BEGIN INSERT INTO results VALUES (2, :x); DECLARE x INTEGER := 100; BEGIN INSERT INTO results VALUES (3, :x); END; INSERT INTO results VALUES (4, :x); END; INSERT INTO results VALUES (5, :x); END;
SELECT value FROM results ORDER BY seq
